info.title: GePG Bridge: billing system API
info.description: Send bills to GePG through the bridge and get told when they are approved or paid. Events are described under webhooks.

ApiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
ApiKeyAuth.description: Send your API key in the X-Api-Key header on every call. Keys are issued per billing system.

get.description: Returns the billing system your API key belongs to. Use it as the first call when setting up.

post.summary: Create a bill and send it to GePG
post.description:
Saves the bill and sends it to GePG. GePG answers in two steps: an immediate acknowledgement (this response) and, a moment later, the control number as a bill.approved event.

A 201 means GePG received the bill, not that it approved it. Wait for the bill.approved or bill.rejected event, or check the status.

get.description: Your events in order, oldest first. Keep the nextCursor of the last batch you processed and ask for what came after it. Use this to catch up after downtime, or as your whole integration if you have no callback URL.

parameters.description: Cursor: only events after this one. Start with 0.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Events per call, 1 to 500. Defaults to 100.

post.description: GePG accepted the bill. It now has a control number the payer can use.

parameters.name: X-Bridge-Event
parameters.description: The event type.

parameters.name: X-Bridge-Event-Id
parameters.description: The event number. The same event can arrive more than once, so remember the ids you have handled.

parameters.name: X-Bridge-Delivery-Attempt
parameters.description: 1 for the first try, 2 for the first retry, and so on.

parameters.name: X-Bridge-Timestamp
parameters.description: When this attempt was signed, in unix seconds.

parameters.name: X-Bridge-Signature
parameters.description: How to check the sender: t=<timestamp>,v1=<signature>. See "Check the signature".

200.description: Accepted. Any 2xx status confirms delivery; the body is ignored.
